mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS <= 0.2%) is a condition that is always true, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of instances despite FEDFUNDS <= 0.2%, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeds 9.0%, it signals a weak labor market that is likely to prompt further monetary policy easing, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of instances when UNRATE > 9.0, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in labor market participation (PAYEMS < 132000) and contraction in real GDP (GDPC1 < 113500) indicates a deepening economic slowdown, which triggers a flight to safety and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite PAYEMS < 132000 AND GDPC1 < 113500, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During a recessionary regime defined by unemployment rate above 8.0% and negative real GDP growth (GDPC1 growth < 0%), the Federal Reserve typically implements aggressive monetary easing, which supports equity market recovery and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of instances during UNRATE > 8.0 AND GDPC1 growth < 0%, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO < 98.0) signals a contraction in the manufacturing sector, which is associated with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5d returns in > 60% of instances when INDPRO < 98.0, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL > 212.5) indicates accelerating inflation, which typically leads to a tightening of monetary policy and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 212.5, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts (HOUST < 460.0) signals a weakening real estate market, which is a leading indicator of economic contraction and results in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5d returns in > 60% of instances when HOUST < 460.0, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Strong retail sales (RSAFS > 340000) indicate robust consumer spending, which is a key driver of economic growth and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 60% of instances despite RSAFS > 340000, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
